title: Canadian Wildfires and Trump Policies
author: George Wuerthner
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/detroitsmoke-680x514.png)

Smoke from Canadian wildfires has occasionally led to hazardous air conditions
in major US cities.

As smoke from wildfires in Canada billowed across the central and eastern
parts of the United States, President Trump once again demonstrated his utter
ignorance of wildfire ecology.

[Detroit on Friday remained the most polluted city in the
world](https://substack.com/redirect/ef7a7b6a-3e38-4cbb-b5af-f58bb7662229?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg),
according to tracker IQAir. Other major cities like Washington DC and Chicago
were equally polluted.

[Trump
declared](https://substack.com/redirect/0d620c1c-e693-495e-ab86-87a4f1b31eac?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg):
“We are holding Canada responsible,” he wrote, “for the fact that they are not
properly maintaining their Forests, and Brush therein, and the United States
is being unnecessarily invaded by filthy, polluted, and unhealthy air, the
quality of which is dangerous, and totally unacceptable!”

Trump suggested that he will increase tariffs on Canada to pay for the
“willful negligence” ensuring even more animosity towards the US from our best
neighbors and allies. Will Trump increase tariffs this winter if a “polar
express” sweeps out of the Arctic and across the US driving up heating costs?
I am surprised he hasn’t immediately [shipped more
rakes](https://substack.com/redirect/a23be2eb-2f53-49b8-8dac-c243acaaae00?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg)
to Canada so they can clean up their forests and make them tidy.

All cynical comments aside, Trump’s response demonstrates how clearly he fails
to understand the relationship between fossil fuel burning, [warming
climate](https://substack.com/redirect/b824f148-88f0-4447-9983-4ca835b5345a?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg)
and wildfires. He has repeatedly declared that climate warming is a “hoax.”

Worse for the planet, his energy policies that promote fossil fuels are
willfully increasing climate warming.

The first problem with Trump’s irrational response is his failure to
understand the scope of the wildfire issue. Canada’s boreal forest encompasses
1.3 billion acres. That’s almost the size of the lower 48 states combined (1.9
billion). Thus far, wildfires have burned 7 million of Canada. Across most of
this vast area there are no roads, not even much forestry. It is impossible to
have any substantial impact on wildfires burning across such a huge area.

Second, wildfires are a natural part of the boreal forest. These forests do
burn on occasion when conditions are “ripe” And those conditions include
drought, high temperatures, low humidity and wind. All those conditions exist
across much of Canada today.

Third, though high severity burns release carbon into the atmosphere, which is
one factor driving climate warming, much of the carbon in burnt forests
[remains locked up in snags, roots and
charcoal](https://substack.com/redirect/e15eb04a-11fa-4e88-b3bd-0d140fc406c0?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg).

By contrast, logging and wood products production, which Trump is proposing,
should be increased both in Canada and here in the United States, releasing a
far higher percentage of the carbon locked in forests. For instance, in
[Oregon](https://substack.com/redirect/4d1f3882-304d-405a-8018-cbd63ce61404?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg),
the Wood Products Industry releases more carbon than all the transportation
sectors in the state.

Plus, there are [substantial economic and ecological
costs](https://substack.com/redirect/8e305289-5bdb-4a59-9d59-fccfda4f6ae9?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg)
associated with logging that are often ignored.

However, the other major problem with Trump’s cognitive dissidence is his
energy policies. Trump has basically unleashed massive new inputs of carbon
from burning fossil fuels.

He has attacked [energy
efficiency](https://substack.com/redirect/57425ca9-5466-42b4-bfc3-94161af7583b?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg)
requirements of the transportation sector. He has
[canceled](https://substack.com/redirect/62f39d64-b03f-4670-91af-a36017254149?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg)
wind energy and solar projects. He has supported [elimination of tax
incentives](https://substack.com/redirect/d35e0853-7040-41d6-a84b-8611869e2107?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg)
to support electric automobile conversion, solar energy on homes, energy
conservation measures in building construction and other renewable energy
policies.

According to a report by the [Bluegreen
](https://substack.com/redirect/62f39d64-b03f-4670-91af-a36017254149?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg)Alliance,
223 clean manufacturing, energy, and industrial projects across the
country—representing at least $82.8 billion in capital investment—have been
canceled or stalled.

Trump is even paying [2\. 3 billion of taxpayer
dollars](https://substack.com/redirect/62f39d64-b03f-4670-91af-a36017254149?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg)
to cancel wind farm projects.

Worse for American consumers, his unnecessary War in Iran has driven up energy
costs for all Americans. While he gloats that America is the [largest producer
of crude
oil](https://substack.com/redirect/f9d98d23-eab0-40e1-b75d-623935dbe27e?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg),
implying this will result in lower gas and energy costs, it ignores the basic
economic reality that the global market sets oil and gas prices. Energy
producers in the United States may produce a lot of oil and gas, but they sell
it at the global price. And that price has risen due to the [uncertainty about
oil supplies resulting from the Iranian
War](https://substack.com/redirect/35900c18-6308-4a5e-98be-c2c04368d126?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg).

There is evidence from over [millions of
years](https://substack.com/redirect/4d0c3e01-f081-45b7-a405-5ea582b606f6?j=eyJ1IjoiYnpudyJ9.InlTuPXTgg90MChcZaIlDtd6mDoH1w3XGFKcjEcxokg)
that adding carbon, whether from natural sources or human emissions, can
increase wildfires. If we continue to release carbon into the atmosphere, we
can anticipate large wildfires.
